Rachel (PMM): Hey @Kevin — quick data ask to close out the webinar story. We want a short evidence pack to back the latency/cost bullets in the launch post. Minimal: sample payloads, aggregated metrics (median, p95, p99), and a one-paragraph note on how the numbers were collected. Can runtime produce this by EOD tomorrow?

Kevin (eng-runtime): Yep, we can. Can you confirm the model variant(s) and traffic shape you want? Also: do you want quantized results or just FP16 baseline?

Rachel (PMM): Thanks. Primary slide uses the open-llm-v2 model (v2.3) and we call out a quantized offering in a footnote — so both would be ideal but baseline FP16 is highest priority. Traffic: mix of interactive chat (short prompts ~20-60 tokens) and long-context generation (~1k tokens) — we can attach the sample prompts.

Olga (data-eng): I can extract an anonymized 2k sample across the two tails (short chat / long gen). Prefer timeframe: last 7 days of traffic to capture recent kernel changes?

Rachel (PMM): Last 7 days works. Include bucketed length distribution and seed ids so we can reproduce a few examples if needed.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Cool. For clarity, acceptance criteria from runtime side: we’ll provide CSV with columns [payload_id, model_version, quant_flag, input_len, output_len, tokens_generated, latency_ms, cost_units_estimated], plus an aggregate summary (count, median, p95, p99, mean). We’ll also note warmup state (cold/warm run) and whether KV cache was used. Is that sufficient?

Marco (marketing ops): Please add sample curl + JSON payloads we can paste into the press playbook, and a short one-liner describing the workload (so docs folks can reuse).

Jules (research): Also request: include any notable outliers and a quick blurb if we had to fallback to a smaller model variant during the window. If there are obvious regression cases vs prior baseline, flag them.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Understood. I’ll schedule a reproducible sweep: FP16 baseline then 8-bit quantized variant with identical seeds. Will capture per-request tracing for 50 random samples and full aggregates for the 2k sample.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Example command I’ll run for the reproducible slice:
```bash
./run_repro_sweep --model open-llm-v2:2.3 --seed-file sample_ids.txt --quantize none --out results_fp16.csv
./run_repro_sweep --model open-llm-v2:2.3 --seed-file sample_ids.txt --quantize int8 --out results_int8.csv
```

deploy-bot: Scheduled job created: job-id=run-1769854321-01, ETA ~3h.

Olga (data-eng): I’ll drop the sample file in /shared/marketing/samples/webinar_1769854321.csv and give read perms to the runtime team.

Rachel (PMM): Amazing — thank you all. Two tiny asks: 1) include a short plain-English paragraph we can use in the slide footnote describing the measurement method, and 2) annotate which numbers are warmup-normalized vs raw.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Will do both. If anything blocks, I’ll ping here. Otherwise expect the artifact bundle + README in the shared folder once the jobs finish. :thumbsup:

Marco (marketing ops): Thanks — we’ll hold the final slide lock until we have the artifacts. If the numbers shift materially, we’ll adjust the headline.

Rachel (PMM): Perfect. Appreciate the fast turn.
